proof:
Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: Step 5 of the parent proof = the printed paragraph before (2) in the "Proof of 8.2" ("since 0⨯∂T_j has boundary ∂T_j … 0⨯∂T_j ⇀ 0⨯∂T … ∂T is integer multiplicity (by the inductive hypothesis) we thus see that the general case of the theorem follows from the special case when ∂T = 0"), together with the cone construction of (P3) (Simon 2.25–2.27, 2.30–2.31, 3.2(2), 3.10, with 3.9 through the sibling push-forward); copied and filled in. Book n = m + 1; the boundaries ∂T_j have degree m (m = 0 allowed).

Hypotheses: LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity; (BLI) for Y_j, Y ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P): if every ∂Y_j is i.m., sup_j M(∂Y_j) < ∞ and ∂Y_j ⇀ ∂Y, then ∂Y is i.m.; (Cyc) the integrality statement for i.m. cycles of degree m+1 on ℝ^P supported in a fixed compact set with bounded masses; K ⊆ ℝ^P compact; T_j, T ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with T_j, ∂T_j i.m., spt T_j ⊆ K, Λ := sup_j (M(T_j) + M(∂T_j)) < ∞, T_j ⇀ T. Goal: T is i.m.

Facts used. (F1) |Z(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M_W(Z) if tsupport ω ⊆ W. (F2) If η, η′ agree on an open set containing spt Z then Z(η) = Z(η′) (partition of unity on the zero region). (F3) For x ∈ ℝ^P and a j-covector α (j ≥ 1), the (j−1)-covector x⌟α := α(x, ·,…,·) satisfies |x⌟α| ≤ |x||α| (the Euclidean coefficient norm is invariant under orthogonal changes of basis; in an orthonormal basis with first vector x/|x|, x⌟α consists of |x| times those coefficients of α whose index contains 1). (F4) If spt Z_j ⊆ K for all j and Z_j ⇀ Z, then spt Z ⊆ K: for tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅, Z_j(ω) = 0 by (F2), hence Z(ω) = 0.

Part I: the cone. For an m-current X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) with compact support define the cone 0⨯X ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) by
   (0⨯X)(ω) := X(ζ·Hω), (Hω)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^m (x⌟ω(tx)) dt,
where ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of spt X. Hω is a C^∞ m-form (differentiation under the integral sign), ζHω ∈ D^m(ℝ^P), and by (F2) the value does not depend on ζ.
1. (Current.) 0⨯X is linear in ω, and sequentially continuous: if ω_l → 0 in D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), then ζHω_l → 0 in D^m(ℝ^P) (supports in tsupport ζ; every derivative of Hω_l on tsupport ζ is controlled by finitely many derivatives of ω_l on a fixed compact set), so X(ζHω_l) → 0.
2. (Boundary.) Suppose X = ∂Y for some Y ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, and take ζ = 1 also near spt Y. Then ∂(0⨯X) = X. For φ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P): ∂(0⨯X)(φ) = X(ζH(dφ)).
   - If m ≥ 1: the radial homotopy formula H(dφ) + d(H′φ) = φ holds, with (H′φ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{m−1}(x⌟φ(tx)) dt (Cartan's formula for the homotopy (t,x) ↦ tx between the constant map 0 and the identity; the term from the constant map vanishes in degree m ≥ 1; this is the form version of Simon 2.25–2.26, 2.31). Hence X(ζHdφ) = X(ζφ) − X(d(ζH′φ)) + X(dζ ∧ H′φ) = X(φ) − ∂X(ζH′φ) + 0 = X(φ), using (F2) twice (ζφ = φ and dζ ∧ H′φ = 0 near spt X) and ∂X = ∂∂Y = 0.
   - If m = 0: H(dφ)(x) = ∫_0^1 dφ(tx)(x) dt = ∫_0^1 (d/dt)φ(tx) dt = φ(x) − φ(0), so ∂(0⨯X)(φ) = X(ζφ) − φ(0)X(ζ) = X(φ) − φ(0)Y(dζ) = X(φ), since dζ = 0 near spt Y (F2).
3. (Mass and support.) If spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) then M(0⨯X) ≤ R·M(X) and spt(0⨯X) ⊆ B̄_R(0). Indeed, by (F3), |Hω(x)| ≤ |x|‖ω‖∫_0^1 t^m dt ≤ |x|‖ω‖. For δ > 0 choose ζ with tsupport ζ ⊆ B_{R+δ}(0); then by (F1), |(0⨯X)(ω)| ≤ ‖ζHω‖M(X) ≤ (R+δ)‖ω‖M(X); let δ ↓ 0. If tsupport ω ∩ B̄_R(0) = ∅, then ω = 0 on B̄_{R+δ}(0) for some δ > 0, hence (tx ∈ B̄_{R+δ}(0) for |x| ≤ R + δ, t ∈ [0,1]) Hω = 0 on B̄_{R+δ}(0), and with tsupport ζ ⊆ B_{R+δ}(0) we get (0⨯X)(ω) = 0.
4. (Weak continuity.) If X_j ⇀ X and spt X_j, spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0), then 0⨯X_j ⇀ 0⨯X: use one ζ (= 1 near B̄_R(0)) for all of them; (0⨯X_j)(ω) = X_j(ζHω) → X(ζHω).
5. (Integer multiplicity.) If X is i.m. then 0⨯X is i.m. Identify ℝ × ℝ^P with ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1) isometrically ((t,x) ↦ (t,x_1,…,x_P)), e_0 := (1,0). For an (m+1)-form η on ℝ × ℝ^P let α_η(t,x) be the m-covector on ℝ^P given by α_η(t,x)(v_1,…,v_m) := η(t,x)(e_0, (0,v_1), …, (0,v_m)). The product current Π := [[(0,1)]] × X ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) (Simon 2.18–2.20) is Π(η) := ∫_0^1 X(α_η(t,·)) dt (t ↦ α_η(t,·) is a continuous path in D^m(ℝ^P), so the integrand is continuous; Π is linear, and sequentially continuous: if η_l → 0 in D^{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) then sup_{t∈[0,1]} |X(α_{η_l}(t,·))| → 0, since otherwise there would be t_l with |X(α_{η_l}(t_l,·))| ≥ ε while α_{η_l}(t_l,·) → 0 in D^m(ℝ^P)). If X = τ(M,θ,ξ) is i.m., then Π = τ((0,1) × M, θ∘π_2, e_0 ∧ ξ∘π_2) is i.m. (Simon 3.2(2)): (0,1) × M is countably (m+1)-rectifiable (products of Lipschitz images are Lipschitz images: (0,1) × F_j(ℝ^m) ⊆ (id × F_j)(ℝ^{1+m}), and (0,1) × M_0 is H^{m+1}-null); H^{m+1}⌞((0,1) × M) = L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^m⌞M (product formula for Hausdorff measure on rectifiable sets, Federer 3.2.23); so Π(η) = ∫_{(0,1)×M} θ(x)⟨η(t,x), e_0 ∧ ξ(x)⟩ dH^{m+1} by Fubini, since ⟨η, e_0 ∧ ξ⟩ = ⟨α_η, ξ⟩; θ∘π_2 is positive integer valued and locally integrable; and for a.e. (t,x) ∈ (0,1) × M the weighted tangent space of ((0,1) × M, θ∘π_2) is ℝe_0 ⊕ T_x (blow-ups of the product are products of blow-ups; apply the tangent property of (M,θ) at x to y ↦ ∫ f(s,y) ds, f ∈ C_c), oriented by e_0 ∧ ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector(e_0, τ) for an orthonormal τ spanning T_x.
   Let h : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ^P, h(t,x) := t x (C^∞). spt Π ⊆ [0,1] × spt X is compact, so h⁻¹(K) ∩ spt Π is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. By `iwl_smooth_pushforward` (with k := m, U := ℝ^{P+1}, V := ℝ^P, the hypothesis LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity) there is an i.m. S ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with S(ω) = Π(η) whenever η agrees with h^#ω near spt Π. Since Dh(t,x)(s,w) = s x + t w, we get α_{h^#ω}(t,x) = t^m (x⌟ω(tx)). Take η := (ϑ⊗ζ)·h^#ω with ϑ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ), ϑ = 1 near [0,1], and ζ as above; η = h^#ω near [0,1] × spt X ⊇ spt Π. Then S(ω) = ∫_0^1 X(ζ t^m (·⌟ω(t·))) dt = X(ζHω) = (0⨯X)(ω); the exchange of X and ∫_0^1 dt holds because the Riemann sums of the continuous path t ↦ ζ t^m(·⌟ω(t·)) in D^m(ℝ^P) converge to ζHω in the test-form topology (supports in tsupport ζ, uniform convergence of all derivatives) and X is linear and sequentially continuous. Hence 0⨯X = S is integer multiplicity.

Part II: reduction to cycles.
6. (∂T is i.m.) ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T (`WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary`), ∂T_j is i.m. for every j, and sup_j M(∂T_j) ≤ Λ. By (BLI) with Y_j := T_j, Y := T, ∂T is i.m.
7. (Supports.) spt ∂T_j ⊆ spt T_j ⊆ K, spt T ⊆ K and spt ∂T ⊆ K ((F4), (F2)). Let R_K := sup_{x∈K}|x| (0 if K = ∅) and K′ := B̄_{R_K}(0) ⊇ K (compact).
8. (Cones.) C_j := 0⨯∂T_j and C := 0⨯∂T (Part I with X = ∂T_j = ∂(T_j), resp. ∂T = ∂(T), Y := T_j resp. T compactly supported). By Part I: C_j, C are i.m. (5; ∂T_j and ∂T are i.m.); ∂C_j = ∂T_j and ∂C = ∂T (2); M(C_j) ≤ R_K M(∂T_j) ≤ R_K Λ and spt C_j, spt C ⊆ K′ (3); C_j ⇀ C (4, since ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T with supports in K).
9. (The cycles.) Define T′_j, T′ ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) by T′_j(ω) := T_j(ω) − C_j(ω), T′(ω) := T(ω) − C(ω) (differences of currents are currents). Then: T′_j is i.m. (`iwl_im_closure`(c) with a = 1, b = −1); ∂T′_j = ∂T_j − ∂C_j = 0; spt T′_j ⊆ spt T_j ∪ spt C_j ⊆ K′; M(T′_j) ≤ M(T_j) + M(C_j) ≤ (1 + R_K)Λ, so sup_j M(T′_j) < ∞; and T′_j ⇀ T′.
10. By (Cyc) applied with the compact set K′, T′ is i.m.
11. Finally T(ω) = T′(ω) + C(ω) for all ω, with T′ and C i.m.; by `iwl_im_closure`(c) (a = b = 1), T is integer multiplicity. ∎
key_steps: Cone 0⨯X(ω) := X(ζHω) with the radial homotopy operator: a current with ∂(0⨯∂Y) = ∂Y, M ≤ R·M, support in B̄_R(0), weakly continuous.
Cones over integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity: product [[(0,1)]]×X (Simon 3.2(2)) pushed forward by h(t,x) = tx via iwl_smooth_pushforward.
T′_j := T_j − 0⨯∂T_j are integer multiplicity cycles supported in a fixed ball with bounded masses, and T′_j ⇀ T′ := T − 0⨯∂T; (Cyc) gives T′ integer multiplicity.
T = T′ + 0⨯∂T is integer multiplicity by iwl_im_closure.
